subject: Service disruption: interim bridge summary and executive outreach for EverHome
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia@everhome.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, ops@everhome.com
Cc: infra-support@cloudregion.io
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s on inference endpoints - noticing spike

Hi Michael / Redwood ops,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 502 responses across our production inference endpoints starting ~08:50 PT. Error rate went from ~0.1% to 7% in 10 minutes, and it looks correlated with batch requests above 2048 tokens. A subset of requests are timing out at 10s. Our engineering lead is on the thread (ops@everhome.com) — can you confirm you are seeing the same and open a bridge? This is impacting checkouts for a small cohort of users.

Attaching a short log snippet and a screenshot.

Thanks,
Julia
Director, Platform
EverHome
[attachment: everhome_bridge_log_snippet.txt (text/plain)]

From: michael.grant@redwood.ai <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: julia@everhome.com, ops@everhome.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-28T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s on inference endpoints - bridge and immediate mitigation

Julia — thanks for the flag and the logs. I'm opening a dedicated bridge now (BR-8372) and we've triaged to a runtime path that fails under certain large-batch KV cache conditions.

Initial actions (owner in parentheses):
- Open bridge & run live captures (ben.carter)
- Apply temporary routing rule to decline >2048-token batches for affected customer routes (karthik_iyer)
- Ramp up small-instance pool in us-west region to absorb fanout (stephanie_nguyen)
- Collect full traces and central sdks logs for RCA (ben.carter)

I'll post a short interim executive-friendly update for EverHome leadership within 45 minutes. Current ETA to containment with the routing rule is ~15 minutes; full restoral depends on repro and a safe runtime patch.

-Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
[michael.grant@redwood.ai]

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: michael.grant@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: julia@everhome.com, ops@everhome.com
Date: 2027-03-28T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BR-8372 - live metrics and temporary controls applied

Bridge update — ongoing (BR-8372):
- Applied routing rule to reject batches >2048 tokens for affected model variants at 09:28 PT. Reject rate now visible; error rate for EverHome requests dropped to ~0.8% in the last 5m.
- Increased small-instance pool by 30% in us-west at 09:30 PT; headroom looks stable.
- Correlation: failures originate from a specific quantized execution path when KV cache size grows beyond ~1.2GB for long conversation sessions. Repro in staging with a crafted load is in progress.

Requested from customer: please hold any large-batch production runs for the next 60 minutes if possible.

Attaching short packet of metrics and our bridge notes.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: everhome_bridge_log_snippet.txt (text/plain)]

From: Julia Park <julia@everhome.com>

Thanks — appreciate the quick mitigation. Two asks from our end: 1) can you provide a single-paragraph executive summary I can share with our VP of Product and CTO; 2) we'd like an expected timeline for a permanent fix and any potential credit/contractual remediation if production impact continues.

We paused large-batch jobs and will keep them offline until you confirm safe.

Julia

Date: 2027-03-28T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Service disruption — executive interim update for EverHome leadership

Julia / EverHome leadership —

Short executive summary (for VP/CTO):
Redwood experienced a runtime failure impacting a quantized execution path under sustained large-batch, long-conversation KV cache growth. We opened a bridge (BR-8372) and enacted a temporary routing control at 09:28 PT to reject >2048-token batches for the affected model variants, and increased small-instance capacity to stabilize throughput. These mitigations reduced error rates from ~7% to <1% within 10 minutes.

Impact: intermittent 502s for a subset of EverHome production requests between 08:50–09:28 PT; effective containment after mitigations. No data exfiltration; requests either failed or were rejected by routing rule.

Next steps and timeline:
- Short term (now): continue routing control and monitoring. Owner: Ben Carter.
- 3–6 hours: deploy a runtime-safe fallback that avoids the failing execution path for large-kv sessions; will be tested in canary and rolled gradually. Owner: Karthik Iyer.
- 24–48 hours: targeted patch to quantized kernel selection and automated regression tests for large KV sizes. Owner: Runtime team.

Compensation / contractual: we will engage our customer success and billing teams immediately to evaluate remediation/credits if impact window expands beyond the contained period. I will coordinate with your account team for a remediation proposal by tomorrow EOD.

I'll follow with an RCA and postmortem write-up once we complete trace analysis and testing. Attached is a one-page executive slide you can share.

-Michael Grant
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
